data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's signature—'variance reduction across panelists on evidence sub-items' as the mark of genuine gain vs. 'high final-answer agreement with high sub-item variance' as mere compliance—is theoretically unstable. A panel of trained non-experts might show LOW sub-item variance simply because they all identically misunderstand or mechanically apply the checklist items, which is pure compliance, not genuine gain. Conversely, high sub-item variance can coexist with genuine reliability if panelists reach the correct answer through different valid evidence-weighting paths. Counterexample: a panel independently misreads a checklist item identically (low variance) yet is systematically wrong on edge cases; per SRC_003's test this looks like genuine gain, but the panel has no reliability beyond the checklist's flawed encoding.
